correctness.rationale: For every path and initial state, integer height windows obey the exact synchronous successor-contact update. Equality of colors forces equality of 1-Lipschitz integer heights, giving the global-maximum covering radius. Under positive three-color support the increments are bounded, centered and one-dependent, with long-run variance 18 p0 p1 p2 > 0; the functional CLT, Brownian unique argmax and arcsine law imply the weak limit and bounded expectation. With two colors the dynamics is nearest-neighbor infection; longest Bernoulli failure runs give the logarithmic constant. Reflection counts strict endpoint record walks, and local CLT gives the extreme fraction. Standalone direct finite checks corroborate without replacing these arguments.

value.rationale: A natural global synchronization-time observable has a sharp qualitative change under loss of one allowed initial color: fixed full support yields macroscopic random times and a universal arcsine law, while exactly two colors yield logarithmic nearest-neighbor infection times. The explicit diffusion coefficient explains the singular support boundary; the exact Motzkin-prefix count quantifies rare diameter-saturating states. These results are reproducible infinite-family and asymptotic statements with clear model motivation, not an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of the diameter bound.
